purpose: Generate editorial topics and classify their target audiences; this does not require personal profiles or evaluate the capabilities of downstream execution agents.

source_files.purpose: Reference material covering role responsibilities, 42 industry segments, and task and output analysis for 546 combinations
Input aliases and legacy-value mappings from the existing implementation, checked item by item against the XLSX source

evidence_status: Input enums retain the source table values, and the industry scope follows the provided research. Content perspectives, task decomposition, grouping, and matching rules are an initial design and are not claimed to have been validated by user click data.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around responsibilities for product functions, structures, materials, and architecture.
role_perspectives.boundary: Includes design specifications and component trade-offs; assign production-batch control to process_engineering.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Compare component options that satisfy the same product specification.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around manufacturing flows, process windows, yield, and scale-up responsibilities.
role_perspectives.boundary: Includes production consistency; assign discussions limited to component function or structure to product_design.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Compare process improvements that reduce interconnect manufacturing defects.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around interfaces, component coordination, and end-to-end system operation.
role_perspectives.boundary: Includes hardware-software compatibility and system validation; assign the lifetime of a single component to reliability_engineering.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Compare interface options between a sensor and a controller.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Review a single material mechanism without any system relationship.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around failure, service life, environmental tolerance, and repeatable operation.
role_perspectives.boundary: Includes failure recovery and lifetime validation; assign purely scientific mechanism contributions to applied_research or scientific_contribution.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Compare connector-structure improvements for thermal-cycling failures.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Evaluate only the novelty of a research paper.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around the technical distinctions, prototypes, and disclosure evidence for an invention concept.
role_perspectives.boundary: May apply to employed engineers; it does not imply independent-inventor status or patentability.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Plan a minimum validation for a new sampling architecture.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Assert without evidence that the user is an independent inventor.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around whether mechanisms, materials, or methods can explain and improve a specific application.
role_perspectives.boundary: Focuses on translatable research evidence; do not infer employer type, and assign production-operations optimization to process_engineering.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Study how noise mechanisms affect imaging performance.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Create only a production scheduling plan.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around research gaps, testable questions, and contributions relative to prior work.
role_perspectives.boundary: Do not infer an academic affiliation; assign work serving only product-function trade-offs to product_design.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Identify a testable gap in low-data reconstruction research.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Assume the user is a university researcher.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around experimental design, measurement, benchmarks, and result reproducibility.
role_perspectives.boundary: Includes comparisons of research methods; frame product acceptance planning from a product or reliability perspective.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Compare experimental methods for testing a mechanistic hypothesis.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around external technology supply, maturity, and adoption conditions.
role_perspectives.boundary: Includes partnership candidates and pilot thresholds; assign customer positioning to product_strategy.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Screen packaging technology paths suitable for a pilot.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around target customers, use cases, product positioning, and feature priorities.
role_perspectives.boundary: Includes market-entry paths; assign external technology-supplier screening to technology_scouting.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Compare initial use cases for launching a new detection platform.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around competitor capabilities, technology changes, and relative positioning.
role_perspectives.boundary: May use technology or patent evidence; the focus is comparison among organizations rather than parameter trade-offs for one solution.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Track the packaging R&D directions of different companies.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around the coverage, positioning, and maintenance of technology assets against business roadmaps.
role_perspectives.boundary: A specific portfolio analysis requires a defined asset scope; it is not an infringement assessment for a single product.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Relate a product technology roadmap to patent-topic coverage.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Conclude from patent counts alone that no infringement risk exists.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame risk questions around product implementation, claims, legal status, and applicable scope.
role_perspectives.boundary: General content may provide an evidence checklist; it must not treat search results as a definitive legal conclusion.
role_perspectives.positive_example: List the claim evidence needed to assess a design change.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Declare FTO clearance without defining the product and jurisdiction.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around R&D collaboration, data use, ownership of results, and transaction responsibilities.
role_perspectives.boundary: Requires an explicit collaboration or contract context; do not treat every Legal user as a patent attorney.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Organize the business inputs needed to determine ownership of collaborative R&D results.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Present an ordinary technology-path comparison as contract review.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around search coverage, family dates, classifications, and feature-to-evidence mapping.
role_perspectives.boundary: The focus is auditable evidence; the perspective does not imply professional representative status or legal advice.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Design a reproducible patent-search strategy for microfluidic cartridges.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Treat a highly relevant result as proof of infringement.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around disclosure support, application documents, claims, and office-action responses.
role_perspectives.boundary: When specific disclosure or prosecution materials are unavailable, generate a template only and do not invent application content.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Use a disclosure-support table to review draft claims.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Invent a specific office action from the industry name.

role_perspectives.definition: Frame judgments around matching technology assets with potential adopters, development gaps, and transaction readiness.
role_perspectives.boundary: Requires an explicit licensing, transfer, or inbound-adoption context; do not infer an active transaction from the user's role.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Identify licensing candidates and missing validation evidence.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Infer a realizable valuation from citation counts alone.

role_perspectives.definition: Help compare possible tasks and deliverables when the task remains unclear.
role_perspectives.boundary: Use only for task_clarification; it is not a catch-all tag for other well-defined tasks.
role_perspectives.positive_example: Explain the different needs addressed by solution comparison and feasibility assessment.
role_perspectives.negative_example: Label a clearly defined search task as unknown.

industry_segments.label_en: Medical Imaging Equipment & Diagnostic Imaging Software
industry_segments.definition: CT, MRI, ultrasound, and software that directly performs image reconstruction or supports diagnosis.
industry_segments.boundary: Hospital imaging services and general wellness applications are excluded; upstream detectors should also be associated with the Electronics industry.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Detectors, imaging chains, reconstruction algorithms, and image interpretation workflows.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Trade-offs among image quality, acquisition speed, and radiation dose; generalization across devices and patient populations.

industry_segments.definition: Clinical diagnostic reagents, instruments, molecular diagnostic systems, and at-home testing products.
industry_segments.boundary: Research-use reagents belong to H13 Life Science Research Tools; hospital laboratory services are not medical-device manufacturing.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Sample preparation, reagent systems, microfluidic cartridges, and signal detection.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Balancing sensitivity, specificity, time to result, and tolerance for use by nonprofessionals.

industry_segments.definition: Continuous glucose monitors, blood glucose meters, insulin pumps, and related closed-loop devices.
industry_segments.boundary: Insulin drugs belong to Pharmaceuticals; nonmedical fitness wearables and general wellness software are excluded.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Electrochemical sensors, skin interfaces, micropumps, and control and alert pathways.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Sensor drift and wearability; transmission reliability, battery life, and validation of drug-delivery safety.

industry_segments.label_en: Surgical Robotics & Minimally Invasive Surgical Systems
industry_segments.definition: Surgical robots, endoscopic and interventional platforms, specialized instruments, and intraoperative navigation.
industry_segments.boundary: General-purpose industrial robots belong to Industrial Automation; hospital surgical services are excluded.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Robotic arms, flexible catheters, wristed instruments, visual navigation, and operator interfaces.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Dexterity and precision in confined spaces; sterilizability, latency, and human-machine interaction safety.

industry_segments.definition: Modified resins, engineering plastics, fiber-reinforced composites, and semi-finished materials; select this segment when the primary business is material supply.
industry_segments.boundary: Coating and adhesive formulations belong to M10; finished automotive or electronic products belong to their respective end-use industries.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Glass-fiber-reinforced thermoplastics, carbon-fiber composites, and low-loss polymers.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Balancing strength, flame resistance, dielectric performance, processing window, and recyclability.

industry_segments.definition: R&D and supply of nickel-based superalloys, titanium alloys, specialty steels, and metal powders.
industry_segments.boundary: Commodity steel trading is not treated as a priority topic; finished aerospace or medical components belong to their end-use industries.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Nickel-based alloys, titanium alloys, and metal powders for additive manufacturing.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Creep and fatigue life, impurity control, and batch-to-batch consistency.

industry_segments.definition: Electrically insulating and thermally conductive ceramics, ceramic fibers, fused silica, and functional glass.
industry_segments.boundary: Construction cement belongs to M14; decorative ceramics and ordinary household glass are outside the current scope.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Boron nitride fillers, low-dielectric glass, and technical ceramic substrates.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Thermal conductivity, dielectric loss, thermal-expansion matching, and brittleness.

industry_segments.definition: Cathode and anode active materials, electrolytes, separator materials, and recycled or regenerated materials.
industry_segments.boundary: Cells, battery packs, and energy-storage systems belong to M05; mining is treated only as an upstream tag.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: LFP cathodes, silicon-based anodes, electrolytes, and recycled materials.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Cycle stability, feedstock impurities, cost, and consistency in mass production.

industry_segments.definition: Motors, inverters, electric drive axles, and hybrid coupling systems for BEVs, HEVs, and PHEVs.
industry_segments.boundary: Battery-cell materials and standalone storage batteries belong to Energy or Materials; chassis and automated-driving systems are separate segments.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Traction motors, inverters, transmissions, and electric-drive thermal management.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Vehicle efficiency, cost, temperature rise, NVH, and compatibility across vehicle platforms.

industry_segments.definition: Perception fusion, driving decisions, control, safety validation, and in-vehicle computing integration.
industry_segments.boundary: General-purpose sensor chips belong to Semiconductors; driver-assistance systems must not be treated as equivalent to fully autonomous driving.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Fusion of vehicle cameras and radar, decision stacks, scenarios, and safety evidence.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Long-tail scenarios, false negatives and false positives, real-time performance, driver takeover, and verifiability.

industry_segments.definition: Braking, steering, suspension, body structures, cabins, and automotive thermal-management components.
industry_segments.boundary: Electric powertrains and ADAS algorithms are separate segments; raw materials belong to the Materials industry.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Body joining, braking and suspension components, and thermal-management assemblies.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Safety and durability, weight, noise and vibration, manufacturability, and supply cost.

industry_segments.definition: Vehicle and systems engineering for road trucks, buses, commercial vans, and special-purpose vehicles.
industry_segments.boundary: Passenger vehicles and fleet-operation services are excluded; off-road construction and agricultural machinery belong to their respective machinery industries.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Vehicle architectures, body-equipment interfaces, power systems, and duty cycles.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Payload, range or energy consumption, downtime, cost, and harsh operating conditions.

industry_segments.definition: Chip design, wafer fabrication, packaging, and testing across logic, memory, analog, and power devices.
industry_segments.boundary: Finished systems, PCBs, and standalone optical instruments are excluded; semiconductor equipment should be classified by its primary equipment-manufacturing activity.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Chip architectures, interconnect packaging, wafer processes, and device reliability.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Simultaneous constraints on performance, power, area, yield, thermal management, and mass-production cost.

industry_segments.definition: PCBs, connectors, passive components, and electronic assembly interconnects, including rigid-flex boards.
industry_segments.boundary: Semiconductor chips, complete server systems, and complete optical systems are excluded.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Multilayer boards, microvias, solder joints, connector contacts, and passive networks.
industry_segments.source_constraints: High-frequency loss, heat dissipation, miniaturization, and long-term connection reliability.

industry_segments.definition: Hardware and systems integration for servers, storage systems, network switching, and communications equipment.
industry_segments.boundary: Pure-software SaaS, chip design, and data-center power infrastructure are excluded.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Server nodes, switches, rack interconnects, and hardware cooling.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Compute density, communications bandwidth, power consumption, serviceability, and supply lead times.

industry_segments.definition: Lasers, optical instruments, imaging and spectroscopic detection systems, and optical sensing modules.
industry_segments.boundary: Chip-level semiconductor devices belong to E01; non-optical sensors should be classified by their actual end-use industry.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Laser sources, optical paths, imaging or spectroscopic sensing, and calibration chains.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Signal-to-noise ratio, resolution, environmental drift, size, and the cost of calibration at scale.

industry_segments.definition: Industrial robots, collaborative robots, machine-vision integration, and automated work cells.
industry_segments.boundary: Consumer robots are excluded; standalone non-robotic processing equipment belongs to a separate segment.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Robot bodies, end effectors, vision systems, and work-cell control.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Cycle time, changeover, worker safety, precision, and the cost of custom integration.

industry_segments.definition: Metalworking machine tools, forming equipment, and specialized production equipment; add customer-specific tags for relevant machinery subdomains.
industry_segments.boundary: Robotics and additive-manufacturing equipment are separate segments; civil construction services are excluded.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Spindles, motion axes, cutting tools, and process control.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Precision, cycle time, thermal drift, reliability, and energy consumption per unit of output.

industry_segments.definition: Industrial 3D printers, process monitoring, control systems, and equipment integration.
industry_segments.boundary: Printing powders and resins belong to Materials; pure printing services should receive additional tags based on the customer's end-use industry.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Printing equipment, powder spreading or energy input, in-process monitoring, and build processes.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Batch-to-batch repeatability, defects, surface quality, throughput, and qualification cost.

industry_segments.definition: Engineering analysis, design, technical consulting, and integration recommendations for facilities, systems, and products.
industry_segments.boundary: Equipment manufacturing, construction contracting, general management consulting, and legal services are excluded.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Facility or system concepts, computational models, interfaces, and engineering deliverables.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Customer constraints, design assumptions, verifiability, multidisciplinary coordination, and delivery responsibility.

industry_segments.definition: Monoclonal antibodies, bispecific antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, and other therapeutic proteins.
industry_segments.boundary: Small-molecule drugs are excluded; contract manufacturing belongs to CDMO; cell and gene therapies are separate segments.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Antibody sequences, binding structures, linkers and payloads, formulations, and analytical methods.
industry_segments.source_constraints: In addition to potency and selectivity, aggregation, stability, manufacturability, and safety evidence must be addressed.

industry_segments.definition: Cell therapies such as CAR-T, in vivo and ex vivo gene therapies, and gene-editing therapies.
industry_segments.boundary: Gene editing for nontherapeutic uses belongs to the relevant agricultural or industrial segment; general reagents and pure CDMO services are separate segments.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Cell populations, vectors, editing systems, delivery, and potency assays.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Consistency of cells or vectors, delivery efficiency, potency characterization, and batch scale-up.

industry_segments.definition: Biologics CDMO, cell-line development, culture and purification, analytical testing, and technology-transfer services.
industry_segments.boundary: Proprietary drug discovery belongs to the relevant medicines segment; general equipment sales may also be associated with Engineering.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Cell lines, culture media, bioreactors, purification, and formulation processes.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Scale-up comparability, contamination control, yield, batch consistency, and transfer across manufacturing sites.

industry_segments.definition: Enzymes, production microorganisms, and related formulations for cleaning, textiles, papermaking, and industrial bioprocessing.
industry_segments.boundary: Food ingredients belong to the Food segment; finished renewable fuels belong to Chemical, with Energy used as an application tag; finished polymers belong to Materials.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Enzyme sequences, production strains, fermentation processes, enzyme formulations, and application processes.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Activity, stability under operating conditions, fermentation yield, and cost per unit of application.

industry_segments.label_en: Life Science Research Tools & Laboratory Instruments
industry_segments.definition: Research-use sequencing, single-cell and multi-omics instruments, sample preparation, analytical reagents, and laboratory automation.
industry_segments.boundary: Integrated IVD products for clinical diagnosis belong to H02; biologics CDMO belongs to H07; research use does not imply approval for clinical use.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Sequencing and imaging platforms, microfluidics, reagent chemistry, sample preparation, and analytical workflows.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Sensitivity, throughput, batch effects, sample consumption, and cost per usable result.

industry_segments.definition: Autonomous-guidance farm machinery, precision seeding, variable-rate application, sensing, and agricultural-operation systems.
industry_segments.boundary: Businesses primarily focused on engineering and manufacturing may also be associated with Engineering; crop-production services are not equipment R&D.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Agricultural-machine actuators, positioning and visual perception, operation control, and prescription maps.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Robustness in field environments, positioning accuracy, interoperability among heterogeneous equipment, and investment cost.

industry_segments.definition: Commercial seeds, seedlings, and crop-trait development through conventional and biotechnology-assisted breeding.
industry_segments.boundary: Agricultural machinery belongs to the agricultural-equipment segment; pesticides and biological-control products are not separate segments in this version and may be supplemented with Other.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Germplasm, molecular markers, breeding processes, crop traits, and field phenotyping.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Trade-offs between trait performance and yield; genetic background, genotype-environment interactions, and stability across locations.

industry_segments.definition: Manufacturing of frozen fruit and vegetables, frozen meals, and ready-to-eat convenience foods, with emphasis on processing and preservation.
industry_segments.boundary: Dedicated food-machinery manufacturing may also be associated with Engineering; raw grains, beverages, and cold-chain transportation services are excluded.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Food matrices, microbial control, heat and mass transfer, and freezing or drying processes.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Trade-offs among safety, sensory quality, nutrient retention, energy consumption, and production-line throughput.

industry_segments.definition: Proteins, dietary fibers, enzymes, microbial cultures, functional ingredients, and application formulations for food manufacturing.
industry_segments.boundary: Therapeutic drugs belong to Biopharmaceuticals; industrial-use enzymes belong to Industrial Biotechnology; alternative protein does not represent the entire segment.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Protein fractions, dietary fibers, fermentation cultures, food enzymes, and emulsification or gel systems.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Taste and texture, solubility, nutritional composition, formulation stability, cost, and scalability.

industry_segments.definition: Battery-cell manufacturing, battery packs, battery-management systems, power-conversion systems, and commercial, industrial, or grid-scale storage integration.
industry_segments.boundary: Active materials belong to M04; vehicle powertrains belong to Automotive; this segment does not encompass power generation in general.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Battery cells, storage battery clusters, battery-management systems, and storage power-conversion systems.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Trade-offs among service life, safety, usable capacity, and system economics.

industry_segments.definition: Transformers, switchgear, cables, protection and control systems, and grid-enhancement technologies.
industry_segments.boundary: Generation equipment belongs to its corresponding industry; electricity trading alone does not fit this R&D profile.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Distribution transformers, switchgear cabinets, protection relays, and dynamic line-rating monitoring.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Load growth, insulation aging, fault isolation, and delivery lead times.

industry_segments.definition: R&D and manufacturing of photovoltaic cells and modules, encapsulation, tracking structures, and inverters.
industry_segments.boundary: General wafer-level semiconductors belong to Electronics; upstream resins and glass belong to Materials.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Photovoltaic cells, encapsulated modules, tracking structures, and inverters.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Conversion efficiency, long-term degradation, extreme weather, and levelized cost of electricity.

industry_segments.definition: Electrolyzers, fuel-cell stacks, hydrogen compression and transport or storage equipment, and balance-of-plant systems.
industry_segments.boundary: Commodity industrial hydrogen supply belongs to M11; hydrogen-derived fuel synthesis belongs to M12.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: PEM and alkaline electrolyzers, fuel-cell membrane-electrode assemblies, and balance-of-plant systems.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Service life, intermittent-load operation, precious-metal usage, and hydrogen cost.

industry_segments.definition: Photoresists, wet electronic chemicals, CMP slurries, electroplating additives, and deposition precursors.
industry_segments.boundary: Commodity industrial gases belong to M11; wafer-device and packaging services belong to Electronics.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Photoresists, CMP slurries, electronic-grade cleaning solutions, and electroplating additives.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Nanoscale defects, metallic impurities, process compatibility, and batch stability.

industry_segments.definition: R&D and manufacturing of industrial and functional coatings, structural adhesives, electronic adhesives, and construction sealants.
industry_segments.boundary: Base-resin supply belongs to M01; application and installation businesses should receive an additional service-activity tag.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Waterborne coatings, structural adhesives, thermally conductive adhesives, and weather-resistant sealants.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Adhesion, curing speed, durability, emissions, and application window.

industry_segments.definition: High-purity and specialty gases, air separation, purification, gas distribution, and recovery supply systems.
industry_segments.boundary: Hydrogen-energy equipment belongs to M08; catalysts should not be combined with gases as a single segment.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Ultra-high-purity nitrogen and argon, electronic specialty gases, purifiers, and gas-supply systems.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Trace impurities, continuity of supply, safety, and unit energy consumption.

industry_segments.definition: Chemical-conversion production of sustainable aviation fuel, renewable diesel, bio-alcohols, and synthetic fuels.
industry_segments.boundary: Fermentation-platform R&D belongs to Biotechnology with a cross-industry tag; hydrogen-production equipment belongs to M08.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: HEFA and alcohol-to-jet processes, catalysts, and renewable feedstocks.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Carbon yield, hydrogen consumption, feedstock consistency, certification, and production cost.

industry_segments.definition: R&D and manufacturing of heat pumps, air-conditioning and ventilation systems, water-heating equipment, and building controls.
industry_segments.boundary: Construction and installation should receive an additional contractor or service tag; equipment manufacturers must not be treated as building contractors.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Heat-pump compressors, heat exchangers, refrigerant circuits, and building controls.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Low-temperature efficiency, defrosting, noise, installation cost, and occupant comfort.

industry_segments.definition: Cement, binders, ready-mixed and precast concrete, with low-carbon technologies represented through tags.
industry_segments.boundary: The primary activity is building-material supply or product R&D; on-site concrete contracting should receive a separate activity tag; this segment does not encompass all materials.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Low-clinker binder systems, supplementary cementitious materials, and concrete mix designs.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Early strength, long-term durability, workability, and embodied carbon.

industry_segments.definition: Factory-produced modules and panel systems, structural connections, and integrated mechanical, electrical, and plumbing delivery.
industry_segments.boundary: Distinguish factory manufacturing, design, and on-site installation as separate activities; this segment is not equivalent to property development or the entire construction industry.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Building modules, wall panels, structural connectors, and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing interfaces.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Transportation limits, interface tolerances, structural and fire performance, and installation cycle time.

industry_segments.definition: Water-supply and drainage networks, treatment processes and equipment, water reuse, and infrastructure-renewal projects.
industry_segments.boundary: Water-utility operations, engineering construction, and equipment R&D should receive separate activity tags; this segment does not encompass the entire environmental industry.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Membrane treatment, adsorption media, aeration systems, and water-supply and drainage networks.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Effluent quality, energy consumption, variation in contaminant loads, and continuous-operation reliability.

industry_segments.definition: Aircraft, aviation propulsion and avionics, satellites, and spacecraft components or systems; add this as a named industry under Other, and migrate legacy Engineering users based on their target product or system.
industry_segments.boundary: Airline operations and tourism services are excluded; land and naval defense systems and pure cybersecurity are excluded.
industry_segments.source_technology_examples: Aircraft structures, propulsion or avionics, satellite systems, and their environmental qualification.
industry_segments.source_constraints: Mass and power budgets, reliability, traceability, certification, and supply lead times.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Find adoptable technical solutions for a specified function or problem.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not substitute a broad field survey for a problem-driven search.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Compare identified approaches or solutions under shared constraints and evaluation criteria.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: This is distinct from finding solutions; use research_method_comparison for comparisons limited to research methods.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Start from a defined failure mode or performance failure to identify corrective actions and validation.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: The goal is to restore function; use evidence_synthesis when the goal is only to explain a scientific mechanism.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Adjust manufacturing or operating parameters and workflows to improve yield, consistency, or efficiency.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Exclude work that changes only product positioning or a research question.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Organize evidence on existing approaches, technology categories, and maturity.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Focuses on a static structure; use technology_trend_tracking for monitoring change over time.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Turn user problems and technical capabilities into a testable product or invention concept.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Use research_ideation for questions about scientific contribution.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Determine whether a solution has sufficient basis for implementation under specified conditions and identify evidence gaps.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: When conditions are missing, state conditional judgments; use validation_planning to design the validation work.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Design an experiment, prototype, or test path for evaluating a hypothesis or solution.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not claim that experiments have been completed; use research_method_search when the task is to find a research method.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Map the core questions, research paths, and foundational knowledge needed to enter a new field.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not replace the problem structure with a popularity ranking.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Use existing evidence and limitations to identify unresolved, researchable questions.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Failure to retrieve evidence does not prove absence; use research_ideation to formulate a specific research project.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Find measurement, experimental, or analytical methods for a research question.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not treat a product-manufacturing process as a research method without justification.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Compare the assumptions, sample requirements, applicability, and limitations of research methods.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Use solution_comparison for product technology paths.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Turn research gaps into hypotheses, research topics, and testable paths.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not merely list broad research directions; use product_ideation for concepts driven by product needs.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Build an auditable source set around a defined topic and explain relevance.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Use specialized tasks for prior-art or FTO searches; state the source types in the search scope.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Explain common findings, disagreements, and applicability limits across multiple studies.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not treat patent publications as experimental validation; use evidence_search for a search-results list.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Observe changes over time in scientific questions, research methods, or findings.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Use technology_trend_tracking when commercialization and industry adoption are the main focus.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Track technology paths, performance advances, and adoption evidence over time.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Use technology_landscape for a static inventory and research_trend_tracking for purely academic evolution.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Track changes in the capabilities, R&D, and products of specified organizations or organization types.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: When no organizations are provided, explain the screening method rather than inventing the user's competitors.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Screen opportunities from unmet needs, technical capabilities, and application gaps.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Use licensing_opportunity_assessment when a specific licensing transaction is the goal.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Weigh R&D directions by value, evidence, maturity, and resource requirements.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not invent actual company scores when resource constraints and budgets are unavailable.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Organize patent-positioning evidence by topic, organization, time, and family.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: A patent landscape is not product FTO; use ip_portfolio_planning for decisions about owned assets.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Locate relevant earlier public evidence for defined technical features and a stated search purpose.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: State the search date range; do not automatically draw a novelty conclusion.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Compare specified technical features item by item with earlier evidence and identify gaps.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: A technical distinction is not a patentability conclusion; provide a comparison method when disclosure is missing.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Collect claims and legal-status signals around a product implementation, target scope, and time frame.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: This differs from a prior-art search; when scope is missing, provide a search framework without declaring clearance.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Compare a design implementation or change with relevant claim evidence and identify issues requiring review.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Design-around assumptions require validation; when scope is missing, limit the output to a method and risk checklist.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Organize evidence gaps and action items related to technology use, patents, or ownership.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not automatically expand into contract negotiation or definitive legal advice; use collaboration_terms_review for a specific contract.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Organize patent-application documents and their support relationships from a technical disclosure.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not invent technical features; provide a template when only the three profile inputs are available.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Review a supplied document for technical support, wording consistency, and required revisions.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: A document to review is required; otherwise provide a review template.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Organize core features and a claim hierarchy from a technical disclosure.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not invent invention features from an industry name; use a template when disclosure is unavailable.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Recommend scope, dependency, and wording changes to existing claims and supporting materials.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Provide only a template when the original claims and supporting materials are unavailable.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Map supplied objections and cited references to the application's supporting materials and identify response issues.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not infer office-action content or deadlines from an industry; use a template when materials are missing.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Organize a response and amendment support from a supplied office action and application materials.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Provide only a response-structure template when specific materials are missing.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Relate technology assets, application evidence, and adopter needs to identify transaction-readiness gaps.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Requires a licensing, transfer, or inbound-adoption context; do not invent expressions of partner interest.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Map collaboration goals, results, and data use to contractual business issues that require discussion.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Requires a collaboration or contract context; do not enable it automatically because the role is Legal.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Plan technology-asset coverage, business priorities, and maintenance directions.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: A specific plan requires an asset scope; otherwise provide only a planning-method template.

jtbd_tasks.definition: Help distinguish among tasks, required materials, and corresponding deliverables.
jtbd_tasks.boundary: Do not use it in place of an already well-defined task.

desired_outputs.definition: List candidates, screening criteria, and applicable conditions.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do more than list names; prefer comparison_matrix when candidates can be compared on a common basis.

desired_outputs.definition: Compare multiple options using consistent metrics, conditions, and evidence standards.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not directly rank values measured under different conditions; use assessment_brief for the feasibility of one solution.

desired_outputs.definition: State the problem, proposed improvements, rationale, and validation method.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do more than explain the failure mechanism; use validation_plan when the deliverable consists only of validation steps.

desired_outputs.definition: Organize field coverage and relationships by topic, technology path, or organization.
desired_outputs.boundary: Distinguish technology and patent landscapes by task; use trend_brief when change over time is the focus.

desired_outputs.definition: Describe the problem, the concept's distinctions, its rationale, and minimum validation.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not claim that experiments are complete or patent novelty is established.

desired_outputs.definition: Organize conditions, evidence, gaps, and the basis for further judgment on a defined question.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not present unconditional feasibility or clearance; use comparison_matrix to compare multiple options.

desired_outputs.definition: Specify the hypothesis, samples or operating conditions, methods, metrics, and decision rules.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not present a plan as completed experimental results.

desired_outputs.definition: Present research gaps, specific questions, rationale, and testable paths.
desired_outputs.boundary: Use concept_brief for product concepts, and do more than list popular keywords.

desired_outputs.definition: Map sources and locations to supported technical features or conclusions.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not invent literature or patents; use evidence_review when synthesis is the main purpose.

desired_outputs.definition: Synthesize multiple sources, disagreements, and limitations.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do more than list search results; use trend_brief when dynamic tracking is the main purpose.

desired_outputs.definition: Describe changes, evidence, and implications within a defined time window.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not replace temporal change with a static landscape or present a forecast as an observed event.

desired_outputs.definition: Prioritize candidates against objectives, evaluation dimensions, and evidence.
desired_outputs.boundary: Explain trade-offs and uncertainty; do not create a definitive ranking from arbitrary scores.

desired_outputs.definition: Record risk issues, applicable scope, evidence gaps, and required actions.
desired_outputs.boundary: This is not a legal conclusion without a defined scope; use evidence_table for factual retrieval alone.

desired_outputs.definition: Organize a specification, embodiments, and related patent-application sections from a supplied technical disclosure.
desired_outputs.boundary: Disclosure materials are required; otherwise use document_template.

desired_outputs.definition: Identify issues, rationale, and recommended revisions item by item in an existing document.
desired_outputs.boundary: Text to review is required; otherwise use document_template.

desired_outputs.definition: Organize a claim hierarchy and supporting basis from a defined technical disclosure.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not invent technical features; use document_template when disclosure materials are unavailable.

desired_outputs.definition: Organize a response structure and supporting evidence from a supplied office action and application materials.
desired_outputs.boundary: Use document_template when the specific office action and related documents are unavailable.

desired_outputs.definition: Relate technology assets, adopter needs, development gaps, and transaction readiness.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not invent transaction interest or valuations; use candidate_shortlist for a simple technology list.

desired_outputs.definition: Relate a defined asset scope to business and technology priorities and propose maintenance or coverage directions.
desired_outputs.boundary: A portfolio or asset scope is required; use document_template for a general planning method.

desired_outputs.definition: Help distinguish possible tasks, prerequisites, and corresponding deliverables.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not present it as a user requirement that has already been established.

desired_outputs.definition: Provide fields, structure, completion guidance, and a list of missing materials.
desired_outputs.boundary: Do not present assumptions or placeholders in the template as actual user materials or completed conclusions.

topic_themes.definition: AI applications, value, impact, adoption conditions, and technical challenges in the industry.
Recent technical advances, research directions, and evolutionary trends in the industry.
Explain what a technology is, how it is classified, and the problems it commonly addresses.
The industry's main technology areas, system components, or research landscape.
Shared technical bottlenecks, scaling barriers, and unresolved problems in the industry.
Major paths for improving performance, quality, or efficiency without assuming product-specific parameters.
Compare technology paths, methods, or solution categories using industry-wide criteria.
Identify emerging technologies, new applications, alternative paths, and future innovation opportunities.
Industry-level technical feasibility, evaluation dimensions, and validation frameworks.
Research, experimental, measurement, and evidence-synthesis methods applicable to the field.
Energy efficiency, emissions reduction, circularity, sustainable materials, and environmental impact.
Industry-level safety, reliability, quality assurance, and risk control.
Key participants, technology paths, competitive changes, and differentiation directions.
Patent activity, technology clusters, filing trends, and the landscape of major rights holders.
Prior art, FTO, design-arounds, ownership, and other intellectual-property risks.
General methods for patent applications, claims, and office-action handling.

question_intents.definition: Explain what a technology or method is, how it is classified, and the problems it commonly addresses.
Understand recent changes, major directions, maturity, and likely next developments.
Identify the main uses and applicable scenarios for a technology in the target industry.
Find emerging directions, unmet needs, or value spaces worth exploring.
Organize shared bottlenecks, adoption barriers, evidence gaps, and unresolved problems.
Compare technology paths, methods, or solution approaches using shared dimensions.
Determine whether a direction warrants further validation under technical, implementation, and evidence constraints.
Identify major paths for improving performance, quality, efficiency, or reliability.
Identify technical, safety, intellectual-property, or adoption risks.
Monitor major participants, technology bets, product directions, and competitive moves.
Define the hypotheses, evidence, evaluation dimensions, and next checks required for validation.
Organize evidence, trade-offs, and watch points to support a subsequent choice.

scope_levels.definition: The question covers the entire onboarding industry and does not require a specific segment.
The question is limited to one application segment in the catalog without assuming a specific product or component.

selection_policy.role_perspective_mapping: preferred_not_exclusive; explain a task-driven exception in classification.rationale
selection_policy.task_perspective_output_mapping: perspective and output must belong to the selected task allowed lists
selection_policy.scope_level_mapping: industry requires a null segment; industry_segment requires a non-null segment
selection_policy.technology_terms: specific products, technologies, materials, components, systems, methods and processes remain free text in entities/keywords rather than stable taxonomy enums
selection_policy.scope_assumptions: explicitly record any region, time window, application or constraint added to the idea
selection_policy.execution_scope: stage 1 describes the intended work only; no personal files, permissions, agent skills or execution credentials are required
